extraction.name: Stanford Question Answering Dataset (SQuAD)
extraction.description: A reading comprehension dataset consisting of 100,000+ questions posed by crowdworkers on a set of Wikipedia articles, where the answer to each question is a segment of text from the corresponding reading passage.
extraction.creator: Pranav Rajpurkar, Jian Zhang, Konstantin Lopyrev, Percy Liang
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data collection occurred in three stages: curating passages from high-PageRank English Wikipedia articles, crowdsourcing question-answer pairs on those passages where workers entered questions and highlighted spans in the text, and collecting additional answers for evaluation on development and test sets.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: User-generated content data, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Over the development and test sets, 2.6% of questions were marked unanswerable by at least one of the additional crowdworkers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Project Nayuki's Wikipedia's internal PageRanks were used to obtain the top 10,000 articles of English Wikipedia, from which 536 articles were sampled uniformly at random.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: From the sampled articles, individual paragraphs were extracted, stripping away images, figures, and tables, and discarding paragraphs shorter than 500 characters, yielding 23,215 paragraphs. Articles were partitioned randomly into training (80%), development (10%), and test (10%) sets.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowdworkers were tasked with asking and answering up to 5 questions per paragraph; questions were entered in a text field and answers highlighted directly in the text. Workers were encouraged to use their own words, guided by sample tasks and examples of good/bad questions, reinforced with reminder prompts and disabled copy-paste functionality. For development and test sets, at least 2 additional crowdworkers selected the shortest answering span or submitted without marking an answer if unanswerable.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Daemo platform with Amazon Mechanical Turk as its backend
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human agreement was analyzed by treating the second answer to each question in dev/test sets as the human prediction and the other answers as ground truth, yielding 77.0% exact match and 86.8% F1. Mismatch occurred mostly due to inclusion/exclusion of non-essential phrases rather than fundamental disagreements.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 1 answer per question in the training set; at least 3 answers per question in the development and test sets.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Crowdworkers located in the United States or Canada, required to have a 97% HIT acceptance rate and a minimum of 1000 HITs.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Questions are constrained to span-based answers directly from the passage rather than more interpretative or free-form answers found in advanced standardized tests, and systems are restricted to single-passage context rather than multi-document retrieval.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, development/validation, and testing of machine reading comprehension and question answering models.
